newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb blast on India train kills 20 - officials.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast on India train kills 20 - officials.

text.p: At least 20 people were killed and 61 injured when a powerful bomb exploded on a train in the northern Indian state of Punjab on Tuesday, hospital authorities said.

"From the information that we have received so far at least 20 people have died," Bawa Ram Gupta, a surgeon at the Civil Hospital in Bhatinda, told Reuters by telephone. United News of India (UNI) said the explosion occurred at a railway station in the town of Lehrakhanna. Local officials said the blast took place at about 2 p.m. (0830 GMT).
Bhatinda is about 25 km (15 miles) from the site of the explosion.

"The Civil Hospital in Bhatinda has received 62 patients so far out of whom one is dead and the condition of 10 is very serious," Gupta said. He said the victims sustained fractures, burns and facial cuts. Most of the dead were not brought to the hospital, the doctor said. Patients were still being brought in, he added.
Punjab, one of India's most prosperous states, was rocked by a bloody Sikh separatist insurgency in the 1980s. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.

In August 1995, the state's chief minister Beant Singh was killed when a bomb planted in his chauffeur-driven car exploded. At least seven people were killed in March in a bomb blast in Punjab near a busy railway station.
Local officials said the train was travelling from Bhatinda to the city of Ambala, 150 km (90 miles) to the northeast.
Sikh militants fighting for an independent homeland in the agriculture-rich region have often targeted trains and buses, usually inflicting serious casualties.

More than 20,000 people have died in Punjab since discontent with New Delhi turned into an armed resurrection after Gandhi in 1984 sent troops to flush out militants holed up inside the Golden Temple, the Sikhs' holiest shrine.
